how.title: How BAFO works
how.subtitle: Clear steps for issuers and participants, from launch to award.

tabs.label: How BAFO works for your role

one.title: Create the competition
one.body: Choose a tender or an auction, set the rules and dates, and attach the terms and documents.

two.title: Invite participants
two.body: Invite companies by e-mail or from your vendor directory, and cover their participation fees if you wish.

three.title: Follow offers live
three.body: Offers reach you as they are submitted, with the participant ranking. Closing extends automatically for late offers when you turn it on.

four.title: Award
four.body: Choose the best offer, record the award justification when needed, and download the results report.

one.title: Receive the invitation
one.body: The invitation arrives by e-mail with a summary of the competition and the join deadline.

two.title: Join and review
two.body: Review the terms and documents, and ask the issuer your questions.

three.title: Submit your offer
three.body: Submit before closing, improve your offer within the competition rules, and see your rank when the competition shows it.

four.title: Get the result
four.body: You are notified when the competition closes and when it is awarded.

modes.title: Tender or auction, one engine
modes.subtitle: You set the direction when you create the competition, and BAFO applies its rules precisely in both.

tender.title: Tender
tender.body: For buying goods, services and supply contracts: suppliers compete on price, and the lowest offer leads.
tender.examples: equipment supply, maintenance contracts, transport services.

auction.title: Auction
auction.body: For selling assets, surplus and stock: bidders compete on price, and the highest offer leads.

formats.live: Each participant sees where their offer stands during the competition, as far as the issuer allows, and can improve it until closing.
formats.sealed: Nobody sees the offers before closing, and each participant can revise their offer until the closing time.

modes.bafo_round: After closing, the issuer can open a best-and-final-offer round for a shortlist of participants, each of whom submits one final offer.

sponsored.title: Covered fees for your invitees
sponsored.body: Issuers can cover their invitees' participation fees with sponsored participation passes, so invited companies can join without a plan of their own.

choose.title: Cover everyone or a selection
choose.body: Choose which invitees you cover, and set a maximum number of passes.

badge.title: The “Fees covered” badge
badge.body: A covered invitee sees the badge on their invitation. Nobody else is told.

unused.title: Unused passes
unused.body: The value of unused passes can be returned to you as a voucher after the competition closes.

erp.title: Connected to your ERP
erp.body: Connect BAFO to your system to create competitions, invite vendors and receive results and awards without manual entry.

api.title: Public API
api.body: OAuth 2.0 or API keys, with scopes per connected system and an OpenAPI document.

webhooks.title: Signed webhooks

what.question: What is BAFO?
what.answer: BAFO is a Saudi platform for business competitions. An organisation runs its competition, a tender to buy or an auction to sell, invites qualified companies to submit offers, then awards it to the best offer.

tender_auction.question: What is the difference between a tender and an auction?
tender_auction.answer: In a tender, suppliers compete to supply goods or services, and the lowest offer leads. In an auction, bidders compete to buy what the organisation is selling, and the highest offer leads.

sealed.question: What is a sealed competition?
sealed.answer: A competition in which nobody sees the offers before closing, the issuer included. Each participant can revise their offer until the closing time, and then all offers are opened.

identities.question: Can participants see each other's identities or prices?
identities.answer: No participant sees another's identity. The issuer decides what participants see during the competition, such as their rank or the leading offer.

clock.question: How are last-minute offers timed?
clock.answer: Offers are timed on receipt by the BAFO server. When the issuer turns on automatic extension, closing is extended when an offer arrives in the last minutes, up to a published limit.

sponsored.question: What is sponsored participation?
sponsored.answer: The issuer covers the participation fees of the companies it invites with sponsored participation passes, so an invited company can join that competition without a plan.

plans.question: Do I need a plan?
plans.answer: You need an active plan to issue competitions, and a plan to take part unless the competition's fees are covered. Prices exclude VAT, and new organisations can start with a free trial.

erp.question: Can BAFO connect to our ERP?
erp.answer: Yes, through a public API with scoped access, signed webhooks, vendor import and result exports as CSV and Excel files. The API has to be enabled for your organisation.

mobile.question: Is BAFO available on mobile?
mobile.answer: Yes. The BAFO mobile apps let you follow, join and issue competitions. Plans and payments are handled in the web dashboard.
